effect: Drinking adds water to circulation, and the planned comparison shows ADH signaling decreasing as plasma concentration approaches its usual range. The remaining goal is complete.
reaction: The feedback comparison gives the chapter a useful ending, though it does not explain what ADH stands for.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting ADH to the collecting ducts was most worthwhile: the planned illustration links receptors, water channels and the concentration difference to water recovery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the hormone route to the body felt repetitive because the resulting illustration added little to the preceding explanation of that route.

surprise.text: The final planned picture shows fewer ADH signal marks as plasma concentration approaches its usual range, making the feedback relationship more explicit.

arbitrary.text: The separate nerve-ending and vessel combination had a clear purpose, but it came after ADH release had already been shown, so its placement felt somewhat repetitive rather than arbitrary.

continue.text: I would probably continue for the clear physiological connections, although the mostly sequential, compatible-choice menu offered limited meaningful decisions and ADH remained unexplained as an abbreviation.
